topic: Degraded Performance for Multiple Models: LLM Outage Postmortem Patterns

key_points: Sept 4, 2026: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and xAI all degraded within the same few hours — Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Grok.
Anthropic partial outage 9:23am ET, cause found in ~15 min, closed 12:16pm; separate Claude Sonnet 5 blip after midday.
OpenAI elevated errors on ChatGPT & Codex from 10:43am ET, mitigation ~30 min later, resolution 12:55pm.
Multi-model architectures are sold on resilience but fail on correlation risk: shared cloud regions, network paths, and accelerator supply mean independent vendors are not independent failure modes.
Most firms cannot answer what happened to their service during a 3-hour window when four fallbacks were simultaneously unavailable.
The surviving continuity plan is knowing which processes must run with no model at all + documenting the non-AI path before you need it.
Anthropic (Claude), xAI Grok, and OpenAI (ChatGPT, Codex) hit by near-simultaneous outages Thursday; recovered over several hours.
Anthropic outage hit website, API, Claude Code, Claude Cowork; caused by an infrastructure issue, impact ended 9:16am PT.
Grok outage affected US East & West APIs, web, mobile, and X; SpaceXAI confirmed outage at its Memphis, Tennessee compute center, apologized to impacted compute partners.
OpenAI routing error began 7:43am PT preventing access to ChatGPT/Codex, fix implemented 8:17am PT; later another elevated-errors period resolved after mitigation.
Public info has not confirmed whether the three outages shared a common cause.
Naive math: 99.5% uptime primary adds a second independent provider → simultaneous failure ~0.005%; but real 2026 multi-provider deployments sit closer to 99.6–99.8% effective uptime.
When a hyperscaler region degrades, multiple LLM providers hosted there degrade together; shared CDN/DNS causes correlated latency; new-model launch weeks put synchronized load across all providers.
LiteLLM/abstraction layers hide the happy path but not edge cases: tokenizer drift, context-budget differences, refusal-boundary divergence per provider.
Chunk-size, truncation, and summarization logic must be per-provider or you get silent quality regressions on failover.
AI supply chains fail two or three layers below the risk register, at components nobody bought directly.
Map each layer twice: who supplies you directly and who supplies your supplier (inference provider → cloud region → accelerator → power → materials).
A second model provider hosted in the same cloud region on same accelerators is a partial hedge against one failure mode and no hedge against three others.
a16z survey of 100 enterprise CIOs (Jan 30, 2026): 81% of large enterprises run 3+ model families; enterprises shift from fine-tuning toward routing work across models.
Massive simultaneous disruption hit ChatGPT, Claude, and Grok; analyzes root causes of multi-provider outages.
Positions building zero-downtime LLM failover systems (unified gateway, one key for all models).
Framework: cross-provider health checks, automatic routing on degraded performance, circuit-breaking rather than naive retry.

stats.fact: On Sept 4, 2026, OpenAI (ChatGPT/Codex), Anthropic (Claude), Google (Gemini), and xAI (Grok) all suffered degraded service within the same few hours.
Grok DownDetector reports climbed from fewer than 10 just before 9am to 1,365 by 9:45am (ET), easing to 273 later.
OpenAI's outage started as a routing error at 7:43am PT affecting ChatGPT and Codex; fix implemented at 8:17am PT; another elevated-errors period followed and was resolved after mitigation.
xAI (SpaceXAI) confirmed the Grok outage was at its compute center in Memphis, Tennessee and affected US East & West APIs, web, mobile, and X for about 3.5 hours.
A Jan 30, 2026 a16z survey of 100 enterprise CIOs found 81% of large enterprises run three or more model families.
Real 2026 multi-provider deployments achieve roughly 99.6–99.8% effective uptime, not the theoretical 99.99%+ implied by assuming fully independent providers.

Under EU DORA, financial firms reported 3,383 major ICT incidents in 2025, ~29% originating at a third-party provider; first 19 Critical ICT Third-Party Providers (incl. AWS, Microsoft, Google Cloud, Oracle, SAP) named Nov 2025.

September 3 2026 GPT-6 Astra launch (100k+ GPUs at OpenAI's Stargate, Texas) was followed within ~14 hours by cascading AI service outages across ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Copilot, and Grok across ~70 countries.

angles: The 'redundancy is a sham' angle: multiple providers gave zero protection on Sept 4 because they share cloud regions, network paths, and accelerator supply — independent vendors are not independent failure modes.
Correlation-risk mapping: teach readers to map their providers' shared substrate (cloud region, SSO identity, Tier-1 ISP peering, accelerator supply) to find their real single point of failure.
The non-AI fallback path: the continuity plan that survives is knowing which processes must keep running with no model at all, and having the manual/non-AI path documented in advance.
Multi-model cost is non-linear: two providers is not 2x reliability — it's ~99.6-99.8% effective uptime due to correlated tails, tokenizer drift, and refusal-boundary divergence.
Regulatory convergence: EU DORA / Critical ICT TPTP naming means concentration risk is becoming a compliance issue, not just an engineering one.
Postmortem patterns: recognize the recurring causal fingerprints — compute-center failure, routing error, launch-induced synchronized load, SSO/identity deadlock — to triage faster.
